headline: 7 top Awami League leaders sentenced to death over July atrocities
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal has delivered a verdict on crimes against humanity during the July uprising, ordering the seizure of assets of several leaders.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal has sentenced seven top leaders of the banned Awami League and its associate organizations to death for crimes against humanity committed during the July mass uprising.

The court ordered that half of the assets of five specific leaders—including Kader, Nachim, Arafat, Porosh, and Nikhil—be confiscated. This includes approximately Tk22.5 crore of declared assets from four of these leaders.
Chief Prosecutor's office stated that the trial was conducted according to legal provisions for defendants who are intentionally fugitive from justice.
Families of the victims of the July uprising have hailed the verdict as 'historic,' viewing it as a step toward justice for those killed and injured during the protests.
The ruling comes as part of a broader effort to hold accountable those responsible for the atrocities committed during the the student-led movement that led to the change in government.
caption:
7 top Awami League leaders sentenced to death for crimes against humanity. Assets worth crores of taka are to be seized.

The International Crimes Tribunal has sentenced seven top leaders of the banned Awami League and its associate organizations to death for crimes against humanity committed during the July mass uprising.

The court ordered that half of the assets of five specific leaders—including Kader, Nachim, Arafat, Porosh, and Nikhil—be confiscated. This includes approximately Tk22.5 crore of declared assets from four of these leaders.

Chief Prosecutor's office stated that the trial was conducted according to legal provisions for defendants who are intentionally fugitive from justice.

Families of the victims of the July uprising have hailed the verdict as 'historic,' viewing it as a step toward justice for those killed and injured during the protests.

The ruling comes as part of a broader effort to hold accountable those responsible for the atrocities committed during the the student-led movement that led to the change in government.

#Bangladesh #Justice #JulyUprising #ICT #HumanRights

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo, Jamuna TV

headline: DU students trample photos of Jinnah and Ghulam Azam at DUCSU
summary: Students from the 2025-26 academic session protested against the inclusion of the figures' photos in the DUCSU museum.
details: A group of Dhaka University students on Tuesday afternoon pasted photos of Muhammad Ali Jinnah and Ghulam Azam on the floor at the entrance and inside the DUCSU museum to trample them.
